newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA exec sees possible Bank Austria bid.
newsitem.headline: CA exec sees possible Bank Austria bid.

text.p: A senior Austrian banker said on Tuesday he believed that Bank Austria might bid for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein.
"I have this news from a serious source, but not from the finance ministry," President of Creditanstalt's supervisory board chairman Walter Freymuth told Reuters.
"Since the source is a very serious one, I must say I believe the news," he continued.
Bank Austria declined to comment on the report, but the bank earlier said it had "no interest" in buying into Austria's flagship bank Creditanstalt.
There was no immediate comment from the office of Finance Minister Viktor Klima.

Freymuth said he thought there was no question that the offer had already been made to Klima since it would require the consent of Bank Austria's supervisory board, which he believed was meeting tomorrow.
A consortium around insurer EA-Generali has so far made the only public bid for Creditanstalt, which has been on the government's sell-off list since the autumn of 1990.
The government deadline for bids is December 16. -- Elizabeth Fullerton, Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
